thread:
incident-bot: PagerDuty -> page fired: PD-INC-000987 capacity_exhaustion: inference-queue backlog exceeded threshold (queue_length=18600, target=500). Auto-escalation to #eng-oncall.

pagerduty-bot: PD-INC-000987 -> triggered; urgency=high; routing -> eng-oncall. Initial policy: autoscaler-fallback.

alex (oncall): acked :raised_hand: I'm on it. grabbing current graphs and runbook.

julie (support): seeing ~40 customer reports in last 3m: 502/504 on generation endpoints, latency 10-20s for streaming. Pushing incident banner to status.redwood.ai.

maya (sre): can you paste the autoscaler logs and last 5 cluster events? This looks like scale stalled not just slow spinup.

alex (oncall): quick snapshot:

```
$ k get hpa inference-deployment -n prod
NAME                 REFERENCE                     TARGETS   MINPODS   MAXPODS   REPLICAS   AGE
inference-deploy     Deployment/inference-deploy   180%/80%  10        200       10         3h
```

and queue metrics from dashboard (last 5m):
- queue_length: 18600 -> 17500 -> 16000 (still rising before mitigation)
- avg_latency: 820ms -> 6.1s (tails to 18s)

kubectl events:
```
Warning  FailedCreate  2m  node-controller  node quota reached for pool inference-pool-us-east-1a
Warning  FailedScheduling  2m  default-scheduler  0/200 nodes are available: 200 Insufficient cpu.
```

alex (oncall): looks like node quota + provider hotspot. autoscaler requested nodes but provider quota/spot capacity is exhausted. autoscaler itself healthy but cloud returns quota errors.

tim (eng-runtime): got it. two quick mitigations: 1) enable fallback to smaller model variant (quantized) to reduce per-token cpu which reduces pressure, 2) temporarily reduce max_batch_size to cut tail latency. We have an automated route to fallback models via routing policy.

ops-bot: Runbook snippet -> https://internal.runbook/redwood/autoscaler/handling-node-quota-exhaustion

alex (oncall): executing manual mitigations now: 1) request temporary node pool increase via cloud CLI, 2) flip routing rule to fallback-model-v2, 3) throttle non-paying test clients.

alex (oncall): cloud CLI add nodes run:
```
$ cloudctl compute instances resize-pool inference-pool-us-east --add 20 --reason "PD-INC-000987 temporary surge"
Request accepted: change_id=chg-2026-07-12-991
```

pagerduty-bot: PD-INC-000987 -> acknowledged by alex (oncall). Escalation timer paused.

maya (sre): I'm going to request a quota increase with infra-ops and open a provider-support ticket, also starting a manual cold-start window to warm kvcaches. tagging infra-ops.

tim (eng-runtime): issuing routing change to fallback model (canary 100%):
```
PATCH /routing/policies/production
{"name":"fallback-hotpath","variant":"fallback-model-v2","percent":100}
```
applied. monitoring token-per-second dropped ~35% in next 30s.

alex (oncall): also applied a temporary rate-limit on non-prod API keys:
```
$ redis-cli HSET rate_limits nonprod_keys 10rps
```

ops-bot: Provider ticket created: ticket#SPOT-77421, ETA initial reply 14m.

pagerduty-bot: PD-INC-000987 -> escalated to SRE lead (maya) after 8m of continued impact per policy.

maya (sre): I'm taking over incident lead. alex — nice work on the manual spinup. can you share the cloud change_id and instance IDs once they appear? I'll coordinate with infra-ops on quota and postmortem owner.

alex (oncall): change_id=chg-2026-07-12-991, first instances provisioning: i-0a1b2c3d i-0a1b2c3e i-0a1b2c3f (partial). provisioning time longer than usual (~4m).

julie (support): customer impact update: after routing to fallback, major customers back to 200 but some long-tail smaller customers still seeing intermittent 5xx's. communicated to Customer Success.

maya (sre): checking tail latencies + queue drain...

```
Metrics snapshot (5m after mitigations):
- queue_length: 18600 -> 5900
- avg_latency: 6.1s -> 1.2s
- error_rate: 7.8% -> 1.1%
```

maya (sre): looks like routing + node add are working. still want provider ticket resolution and quota bump. will keep PD incident open until all pods stable and kvcache warm (~30m).

alex (oncall): filing brief timeline in the incident tracker. handoff to maya for post-incident actions and follow-up with infra-ops and product throttle plan.

maya (sre): taking handoff. next steps: 1) infra-ops to confirm quota increase or permanent pool resize, 2) runtime to run an autoscaler/quotas war test in staging, 3) product to consider circuit-breaker for heavy customers. assigning owners.

pagerduty-bot: PD-INC-000987 -> acknowledged by maya (sre). escalation paused.

ops-bot: Action log:
- 00:00 PD page fired
- 00:01 alex ack + runbook invoked
- 00:03 manual node pool resize requested (chg-2026-07-12-991)
- 00:06 routing -> fallback-model-v2 (100%) applied

- 00:12 visible queue drain begins
- 00:30 incident stabilized; handing to SRE for follow-up

maya (sre): I'm creating the follow-up postmortem and will include remediation: quota alerts, autoscaler behaviour on provider quota errors (fail-open vs fail-closed), and a playbook update to auto-failover routing when capacity < X.

alex (oncall): thanks all. logging final notes and closing operational actions.

julie (support): status page updated: All services restored. Sending customer comms template now.

incident-bot: PD-INC-000987 -> incident marked stable, monitoring.

maya (sre): handing to next oncall (tim) for overnight watch and to validate provider ticket outcome.

tim (eng-runtime): got it, will watch the metrics and run a dry-run of the fallback logic in staging tonight.

maya (sre): Postmortem owner: maya; SEV: sev2; ETA draft: 48h.

alex (oncall): final: root cause preliminary = provider capacity + node quota exhaustion leading to autoscaler unable to fulfil node requests. mitigation = manual node pool increase + fallback-model routing + throttling. follow-ups assigned. :thumbsup:
